What Needs You, on Home, holds the questions you need to answer and the notices that tell you what happened. A question has its answers as buttons, such as File It or Keep The Account, and Dismiss. A notice says what happened: groceries you couldn’t pay for, a commitment you slept through, a welcome to the school. The number beside Home on the menu counts both.

Where To Find It
Home, The What Needs You Panel.
When You Can Use It
From “What Needs You”.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Home and read What Needs You: questions first, then notices.
Press one of a question’s answers to act on it from What Needs You, without opening its screen. An answer does what the same action does on the question’s own screen: File It, on your tax return’s question, files the return just as File It on Papers does.
Press Go There to open the screen a question or a notice is about.
Press Dismiss to take a question off the list without answering it.
Press Mark N Read, at the top of the panel, to mark every unread notice read at once.
Press Show All N, under the notices, to see every unread one before you do: the panel draws the six most important first, and Show The Six Most Important goes back to them.
Press a question’s or a notice’s title to open it: how urgent or important it is, when it closes, and where it sits in the list.

How This Works

The play asks for Emotional Depth, Physical Expression, Vocal Expression, Scene Study and Singing, as its kinds of play do (Tragedy, Romantic Drama). The chair reads every student for it the same way: their fit for the play, with a fifth of it scaled by how much of themselves they delivered in their runs since the last casting, and then a balance for who had the big parts in the School’s last productions. The best read gets the biggest part written for them.

Your 87% delivered comes from The Seagull, Yale Rep, 1 night (100%, counted as 1 night); Carlotta Festival Of New Plays, a School production, 4 nights (84%, counted as 4 nights). A Cabaret or Summer run counts half as much as a School production, each run up to eight nights, and a night missed when you weren’t in hospital counts as nothing delivered. Connecticut treats a full-time student as not available for work (CGS 31-235(b)), so a claim pays only once you’ve left school.
